CausalChain: CTNNB1 mutation in HepG2 cells → impaired HNF4α signaling → immature hepatocyte phenotype with low CYP expression → compromised drug metabolism → overexpression of HNF4α reinstates differentiation → restoration of mature hepatic transcriptome and increased CYP levels → improved in vitro modeling of drug metabolism and toxicity.
Hypothesis: Enhancing HNF4α expression in HepG2 cells will re-differentiate them toward a mature hepatocyte phenotype, thereby restoring cytochrome P450 activity and improving the cells' predictive accuracy for drug metabolism and toxicity studies.
Abstract: HepG2 cells, a widely used in vitro model originally derived from hepatoblastoma, exhibit an immature hepatocytic phenotype characterized by low cytochrome P450 expression and altered metabolic functions. This review highlights how the dysregulation of key hepatic transcription factors, particularly the low activity of HNF4α, in conjunction with oncogenic mutations such as in CTNNB1, contributes to an incomplete differentiation state. We propose that targeted overexpression of HNF4α in HepG2 cells may restore a more mature hepatocyte genetic and proteomic profile, elevating cytochrome P450 enzyme levels and reestablishing robust drug-metabolizing functionality. This reprogramming has the potential to markedly improve the predictive capability of HepG2-based toxicity assays and drug metabolism studies.
